title: What goes into our post-tour follow-up

content.job: Standalone list email. Tell the full exchange from more tours and unanswered follow-up to the client's within-a-week practice and prospective texts. Connect the point to the complete LeadLock system with one reply invitation.
content.body:
Her answer was a distinction she pays attention to on every visit: is her venue the first place this couple has seen, or the last?

That one detail changes what she does next. When she knows hers was the final stop, she gets in touch within a week and asks, kindly and plainly, whether they've settled on a venue or haven't decided. A couple at the end of their search can answer that.

A couple who has just started touring is somewhere else entirely. They're still weighing what they've seen against the visits still ahead, and that question would arrive too early.

**What you notice on the tour is the most useful thing we can shape follow-up around.**

Automated follow-up emails were already in place, and she was still writing to couples herself. She brought up the idea of a text after the tour as well, and I told her we could work that in.

That's how we approach follow-up for venue clients. You're already bringing in inquiries, hosting tours and talking with couples yourself. The emails and texts around that work should draw on what you pick up during the visit, so a couple still comparing and a couple ready to decide each hear something that suits their moment.

LeadLock is the platform where we build your email and text follow-up. Inside it, we set up The Foolproof Follow-Up Advantage, our email-and-text system, around your own conversations. You run the platform, and the personal contact with couples stays yours.
content.ending:
If you'd like follow-up support shaped by how your tours actually go, simply reply to this email and let's talk about your business.

Talk soon,
Whitney

content.title: First tour or last tour
content.script:
I had a call with one of our venue clients recently, and she was booking more tours, but more of those couples were going quiet afterwards.

So I asked her a question. When couples leave a tour, do they still have other venues to see, or are they ready to move forward?

And she explained that she gauges one thing: is her venue their first tour, or their last?

When she knows it's their last, she reaches out within a week and asks, really politely, if they've made their choice or they're still undecided.

I thought that was such a smart distinction.

Because a couple who's just started touring is still comparing, right? They're not necessarily ready for that question yet.

Now, she already had automated emails going out, and she was following up personally on top of that. She'd been thinking about texting couples after the tour, too, and I told her we could add that.

So when we shape follow-up after a tour, the fact that a couple visited is only part of the picture. We want to know what they're ready to do next, so every email and text supports the conversation you're already having with them.

caption.body:
You walked them through the space and answered every question. Then the follow-up starts, and you're writing to couples without knowing whether they're still visiting other venues or nearly ready to choose.

I talked about this with one of our venue clients recently. I asked whether her couples left still planning other visits or ready to move forward. She told me she pays attention to where her venue sits in a couple's search.

When her venue was the last one they toured, she reaches out within a week with a polite, direct question: have they chosen a venue, or are they still undecided? Someone near the start of their search might need more time before that question fits.

She was pairing automated emails with her own personal outreach, and when she raised adding post-tour texts, I agreed we could work them in.

What a venue learns on the tour is our starting point. It tells us what the next email or text should make room for, so the support around your conversations meets couples at the point their search has actually reached.

content.title: Welcome video by text
content.script:
A venue client and I talked about sending couples a short video of her, by text, right after they inquire.

She was already working on a video, and we were figuring out where it should go. I mentioned that inboxes get pretty chaotic, and couples are often more likely to see a text, and actually answer it, than an email. She said that's very true for her couples.

So the idea we talked through was simple. Her first text after someone inquires could link to a video with her on camera, introducing herself and the venue, and then cutting to footage from real weddings, or even a little behind-the-scenes look.

She pictured it as a personal welcome from her, a quick virtual tour right there in the message.

And honestly, I think it could go to everyone who inquires, not only the couples who've already booked a tour.

What I love about it is the job it's doing. It's a sneak peek of what they'll see in person. We even talked about saying it plainly: you need to see this venue before you decide on one.

That's what we want that first message to do. Give a couple a real reason to come see the place for themselves.

caption.body:
They've seen your photos and your website, and they've reached out. The first thing they get back from you is a message, and it can do more than confirm you received their inquiry.

Recently, a venue client and I talked through what that first message could hold. She was already working on a video, and I suggested sending it by text as a link, since a text is often the message couples notice and reply to. She agreed that's true for her couples.

The video we discussed would open with her on camera, saying who she is and a little about the venue, then move into footage from weddings there or a peek behind the scenes. She thought of it as a personal welcome in her first text after someone inquires.

The point is to give couples a preview of what they'll experience on a visit, and a clear sense that they should see the venue in person before they settle on one.

This is the kind of detail we like to work through with venue clients: what a couple hears from you first, and whether it moves them closer to booking a tour.

content.title: The photo inside the text

caption.body:
Maybe it's a warm note and a link to a gallery or a recent wedding on your blog. It's a good instinct, because couples want to see what a real wedding at your venue looks like.

One of our venue clients had exactly that in her first text: a link to a recent gallery of her favorite photos. On a call, I mentioned that some of the venues we work with have started putting photos right into their text messages, so couples can begin to picture it. She said having the photos in the text itself would be even better than the link.

So we talked about including her best photo directly, with a short line inviting couples to see more of that wedding on her blog. I also suggested she think about which photos she'd want paired with her welcome texts, or with the texts couples get once they've booked a tour.

It's a small change, and it comes down to what a couple sees in the first few seconds after they hear from you, before they've tapped on anything.

before_publishing.text:
A line a person wrote for the earlier Reel 3 was not carried into its new premise: More tours are a good sign. But a tour on your calendar doesn't tell you whether the couple is on their first visit or their last, and unanswered follow-up looks the same either way.

This came up with one of our venue clients. I asked whether couples left planning other visits or ready to move forward. Her answer was that she watches whether her venue opened their search or closed it.

When she knows they've finished touring, she reaches out within a week and politely asks if they've landed on a venue or are still undecided. A couple who has only begun visiting is still comparing what they've seen.

She already paired automated emails with her personal contact, and she asked about texting couples after the tour as well. I said we could add that.

That's the kind of detail we want shaping the emails and texts around your conversations, so each couple hears from you in a way that suits how far their search has come.
